messages:
sara (research): Quick heads-up — on the new LlamaX-v2 INT8 bakeoff we see strange activation spikes in a few middle transformer layers, causing ~3.5% ROUGE-L regression on our summarization eval set.

jon (ml-eng): Can you paste the per-layer summary? rough numbers OK

sara (research): Pasting top rows: layer 7 p99.99=2.1, layer 8 p99.99=12.4, layer 9 p99.99=11.8, median activation ~0.6. kurtosis/skew are high on 8/9.

pri (quant): Sounds like classic outlier channels. Did we use per-channel (AWQ) or per-tensor (naive int8)? Which recipe on the bakeoff?

sam (bench): AWQ-int8 with per-channel scales, default clip-by-max. Backend: dedicated-pool-a, runtime v3.2. Throughput ok, but quality hit on summarization and QA.

pri (quant): Two quick mitigation families: (A) surgical rescale (per-channel clamp using high percentile instead of max + floor scale), (B) skip/keep-fp16 for flagged layers. We should measure latency/regressions.

lee (infra): Runtime now supports heterogenous precision per-layer (we expose keep_fp16_layers list). We can ship a candidate that quantizes everything except listed layers.

sara (research): I ran a local probe: skipping layer 8 (keep fp16) reduced ROUGE delta from 3.5% -> 0.7% and increased median latency by ~2.3ms per call on our bench infra. That seems promising.

taryn (product): +2.3ms sounds acceptable for most customers, but we need SLO check for low-latency tier. Also want cost delta estimate.

sam (bench): Cost delta tiny (~+0.5%) since it fits in same GPU memory footprint on our test instance. If we need more fp16 layers memory could increase.

pri (quant): I'll propose a concrete heuristic: compute p99.99 activation per channel; if p99.99/median > 20 => mark layer for fp16; if p99.99/median in (6,20] => per-channel clamp with scale computed from p9999 and floor_scale=1e-3.

jon (ml-eng): Sounds reasonable. Can you share the scan script?

pri (quant): dropping snippet here — rough prototype:

```
python tools/scan_activations.py \
  --model llamaX-v2 \
  --dataset sample_prompts.jsonl \
  --metric p99.99 \
  --out scans/llamax-v2-scan-1785.json
# output rows: layer,channel,p99.99,median
```

pri (quant): Then a small config generator: if ratio>20 -> keep_fp16 add layer, elif ratio>6 -> mark layer per_channel_clamp, else int8.

sara (research): I also tested a rescale-only approach: for layers 8/9, scaling channels by 0.1 for top 0.5% channels + clamp brought ROUGE down to 1.1% delta and latency unchanged. So two viable options: skip-layer or rescale-surgery.

lee (infra): We can A/B both strategies via rollout: variant A = surgical rescale; variant B = skip-layer fp16. Runtime supports dynamic policy routing by model config, so we can compare traces.

sam (bench): I'll run a 100-seed sweep on bench cluster with both variants vs baseline AWQ and GPTQ baselines. Will measure ROUGE/BLEU/QA-F1 and latency p50/p95.

pri (quant): Heuristic thresholds need tuning. For farther robustness add: require at least 3 examples with spike before flagging a layer to avoid noisy single-example spikes.

deploy-bot: scheduled quant-scan job started for llamaX-v2 on bench-cluster at 2026-03-19T09:12Z

sara (research): Nice. For the eval set use: summarization (x2), QA, and a coherence probe. We'll average across seeds and report mean+std.

jon (ml-eng): Timeline: can we have scan + candidate configs by Thu EOD? I can coordinate infra and merge candidate configs into experiment pipeline.

pri (quant): Yes, I'll have scan job and cfg generator by Thu. sam will run the sweeps.

lee (infra): I'll tag a 8x-A10 cluster 'quant-bakeoff-llamax-v2' and grant bench team access.\

sam (bench): Will post top-3 configs and perf matrix into the drive link and ping here.

sara (research): Thanks all — attaching quick notes / CSV to the drive link: drive.redwood/quant/llamax-v2/scan-1785.csv

taryn (product): Thanks team — this is critical for the POC. Keep me posted on regressions and recommended rollout.

pri (quant): one more idea — if we detect recurring spikes across models we should try per-head pruning of the few offending channels during training-time quant-aware finetune. Not for this bakeoff but flagging.

jon (ml-eng): Good call, file a ticket and let's capture for model-onboarding checklist.

sara (research): :thumbsup:"
